summary:
New South Wales issues its own birth certificates and driver licences and runs its own anti-discrimination, conversion-practices and corrections regimes. Marriage and passports are national matters and are carried at the national level.

Discrimination on the basis of transgender status has been prohibited in New South Wales since 1996 under the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977, which reaches employment, public education, goods and services, banking, health care, property and nightclubs. Section 16 of the Mental Health Act 2007 states expressly that sexual orientation and gender identity are not mental illnesses.

The Act's exemptions remain significant for a trans visitor. Sport and broadly based religious exemptions in non-public schools permit exclusion on sex and gender grounds, including barring transgender people from female sports categories, and religiously run adoption agencies may refuse same-sex couples.

Sex designations on New South Wales birth certificates changed on 1 July 2025. Until 30 June 2025 a person had to undergo sexual reassignment surgery and pay $153 to change the sex recorded on a birth certificate; since 1 July 2025 no surgery is required, and the process is an application form, a $73 fee, and a good-faith witness who is an unrelated adult known to the applicant for a year. There is no cap on the number of sex changes, unlike name changes, which are limited to once every 12 months and three in a lifetime; 766 sex changes had been recorded by September 2025. The new certificate does not disclose that a change occurred.

Non-binary and unspecified markers are available. In April 2014 the High Court of Australia held that the law permits registration of a change of sex to a non-specific designation, in the case brought by Norrie May-Welby, and since March 2022 rainbow birth certificates listing no gender or sex have been available to people born or adopted in New South Wales.

Conversion practices have been a criminal offence in New South Wales since 4 April 2025 under the Conversion Practices Ban Act 2024, passed unamended on 22 March 2024. Practices causing substantial mental or physical harm carry up to five years' imprisonment, and taking a person out of New South Wales for conversion therapy carries up to three years. Anti-Discrimination NSW can investigate complaints from 4 April 2025 with civil referral pathways. The Act carries limited religious and parental exemptions, including an exception for religious sermons.

Publicly threatening or inciting violence has been an offence since 13 August 2018 under the Crimes Amendment (Publicly Threatening and Inciting Violence) Act 2018, passed unanimously by both houses in June 2018, with a penalty of up to three years' imprisonment.

Documented fatal violence against a trans woman traveller in the state is the 2021 killing of Mhelody Bruno, a 25-year-old transgender woman from the Philippines visiting Australia, in Wagga Wagga. The perpetrator's guilty plea to manslaughter drew a 22-month term. The most recent documented case of this kind in this record is from 2021; no later instance is documented.

Corrections practice is governed by New South Wales prisoner protocols and guidelines in place since 1996, which permit transgender people who have had sexual reassignment surgery to be housed in female prisons for protection. An undisclosed New South Wales government settlement was granted to a transgender individual held in a male prison in November 2024.

Facilities: Sydney City Council implemented a gender-neutral bathrooms policy in April 2023.
tangentialFactors:
A judicial inquiry into LGBTIQ hate crimes was announced in November 2021 and began work in November 2022, examining 88 deaths of gay men between 1970 and 2000; NSW Police were called to give evidence in December 2022. The inquiry's subject matter is gay men's deaths rather than trans-specific violence, and no trans-specific violence statistics for New South Wales appear in the sources reviewed.

Other official gestures sit alongside the enforceable provisions. A unanimous, non-binding bipartisan lower-house motion in October 2020 called for human rights, dignity and respect for transgender individuals. A ban on Nazi symbols under the Crimes Act 1900 was assented on 19 August 2022 and took effect immediately, with the LGBTIQ community named among those it protects. A government hate-crimes bill concerning gay and bisexual men, with penalties up to five years' imprisonment, was before the parliament in March 2026 and had not been debated in either house.

The state's decriminalisation of private consensual sex between men in 1984, the equalisation of the age of consent to 16 in May 2003, the 2014 expungement scheme for historical convictions and the June 2024 government apology are matters of the state's sexual-orientation history rather than of trans legal status.
localsOnly:
Residents seeking a sex change on a New South Wales birth certificate since 1 July 2025 pay $73 and lodge an application with a good-faith witness who is an unrelated adult known for a year; no surgery is required. Name changes remain capped at once every 12 months and three per lifetime, while sex changes are not capped, and 766 changes had been recorded by September 2025.

Inner West Council in Sydney voted to approve transgender health leave for its staff. The policy has not taken effect because it requires the local government minister's signature.

New South Wales operates a registered partnerships scheme for couples, one of the state-level relationship recognition schemes available across most Australian states.

Anti-Discrimination NSW accepts complaints under the Conversion Practices Ban Act 2024 from 4 April 2025 and can refer matters through civil pathways; complaints on gender identity grounds under the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977 have been available since 1996.
outOfScopeNotes:
No charging or prosecution data for conversion-practices offences under the Conversion Practices Ban Act 2024, or for the public threatening and inciting violence offence created in 2018, appears in the sources reviewed. The number of gender-identity complaints received by Anti-Discrimination NSW is likewise not sourced.

The terms of the November 2024 New South Wales government settlement with a transgender individual held in a male prison are undisclosed, so the precedent it sets for housing decisions is unresolved.

Whether the Inner West Council transgender health leave policy has since received the ministerial signature it requires is unresolved in these sources.

No trans-specific violence rate for New South Wales, with a denominator or against the state's general homicide rate, is available in the inventory; the record contains a single documented fatal case, from 2021, and no count of incidents over a period.

The 766 figure for sex changes on birth certificates is reported as at September 2025 and has no later data point in these sources.
